acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/text returns { content: string, cached: boolean } with content-type: application/json
When no pre-existing .md file exists, the endpoint extracts text, writes a .md file alongside the .jsonl (same directory, same base name), and returns { content, cached: false }
When a pre-existing .md file exists (CLI-generated or prior access), the endpoint reads and returns it with { content, cached: true } without re-extracting
A write error during .md caching does not propagate — the endpoint still returns the extracted content successfully
Invalid filenames (path traversal attempts, non-.jsonl names) are rejected with a 404 response
The .md filename is derived server-side from the validated .jsonl filename — never accepted from user input
The route follows the same guard conditions as the existing /rendered route (SAFE_SLUG_REGEX checks, resolveRepoName, path prefix check)

summary: Reviewed 2 modified files (mcp-server/gui/api.ts — handleGetChunkText, mcp-server/gui/server.ts — route dispatch block). 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (informational — do not block), 2 Low observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS. The new endpoint demonstrates a strong, layered security posture with explicit allowlist validation, server-side path derivation, defense-in-depth prefix checks, ambiguity-downgrade information hiding, and consistent application of existing security headers and CORS controls.

comments.note: No Critical or High security findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed against the new handleGetChunkText() handler and its server.ts route block. Full review summary below.

A01 — Broken Access Control: PASS. slug and repoUrlParam are validated by SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) in server.ts before any handler call, and again by assertSafeSlug() inside handleGetChunkText(). filename is validated against CHUNK_FILENAME_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/) — a strict allowlist that rejects path separators, dots except the .jsonl suffix, and all traversal sequences. The derived mdPath is then checked with startsWith(chunksDir + sep) — a defense-in-depth boundary check so no derived path can escape the chunks directory. No IDOR vectors identified: the route requires a validated (repo, slug, filename) triple and resolves the on-disk path entirely server-side.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures: PASS. No encryption or secrets involved. .md and .jsonl files are plain text at rest and served over a local HTTP server (same trust boundary as all other endpoints in this codebase). No passwords, tokens, or keys are written or read.

A03 — Injection: PASS. No user input is interpolated into shell commands, SQL, template engines, or OS-level calls. readFile() and writeFile() both receive server-derived absolute paths (validated, not user-supplied strings). renderChunksToText() receives raw JSONL file content (trusted disk read) — not user-supplied request body data. The response is JSON-serialised via JSON.stringify() before transmission; the content field is a string embedded in a JSON object, preventing XSS injection through the API boundary.

A04 — Insecure Design: PASS. The .md filename is derived entirely server-side from the validated .jsonl filename (filename.replace(/\.jsonl$/, '.md')). This is the correct design — the client never supplies the cache path. The write-error-swallowing pattern (bare catch block on writeFile) is documented and intentional; it ensures a disk permission error on the cache write cannot take down the read path. No logic flaws in the security-critical flow identified.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration: PASS. All API responses use sendJson() which applies the full securityHeaders() set: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'). CORS is restricted to localhost:{port}. Error messages use generic codes (NOT_FOUND, INTERNAL_ERROR) — file system details are not leaked to callers. Internal details are logged only to stderr.

A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components: PASS (scoped). No new third-party dependencies were introduced by this WP. renderChunksToText() is an internal function from chunk-renderer.ts. The only Node.js builtins used are node:fs/promises (readFile, writeFile) and node:path (resolve, join, sep). No CVE check was triggered.

A07 — Identification & Authentication Failures: N/A. This is a local-only GUI server with no user authentication layer. The endpoint is a read-only text extraction route. No session, token, or credential handling occurs.

A08 — Software & Data Integrity Failures: PASS. The .md cache is written from renderChunksToText() output only — the function processes trusted on-disk JSONL content, not external input. No deserialization of untrusted data occurs. The caching mechanism does not introduce an integrity risk: a corrupted .md cache file would simply be returned as-is (cached: true) — this is an availability/correctness concern, not a security one.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures: PASS. Rejected filenames are logged via console.warn() with the literal (regex-validated-to-be-safe) input echoed in brackets. The warning prefixes ([handleGetChunkText]) are consistent with the existing codebase convention. Filesystem errors that propagate (non-ENOENT on readFile) are caught by the global error handler and logged to stderr. The write-error-swallowing catch block is the one case where an error is deliberately not logged — this is an identified low-priority observation (see below).

A10 — Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): PASS. No outbound HTTP requests are made by this handler. All filesystem access is limited to paths under the resolveProjectStore()-returned storageDir. There is no URL fetching, DNS lookup, or proxy behaviour.

Medium — A09 / Observability Gap: The writeFile best-effort catch block (api.ts ~L1630) is intentionally bare and swallows all errors silently. In a scenario where the chunks directory has unexpected permissions (e.g. after a deployment change or container image rebuild), every cache-miss request would silently fail to cache, causing repeated JSONL re-extraction with no operator signal. Recommendation: add a console.warn() or stderr.write() inside the catch block (e.g. '[handleGetChunkText] Cache write failed for {mdPath}: {err.message}') so disk permission issues are observable in server logs without breaking the read path. This does not block approval — the read path is unaffected — but operators would have no signal of a persistent cache-write failure in production.

Medium — A05 / Information Disclosure (marginal): The console.warn() calls for rejected filenames (api.ts L1585, L1598) echo the raw filename string in the log message (e.g. 'Rejected filename (regex check): \'../secret.jsonl\''). Since CHUNK_FILENAME_RE has already failed at that point, the echoed string could contain attacker-controlled characters (path separators, null bytes, ANSI escape sequences). In a scenario where server logs are forwarded to a log aggregator UI, this could allow log injection or terminal escape injection. Recommendation: sanitize or truncate the filename before logging (e.g. JSON.stringify(filename.slice(0, 64)) to neutralize special chars). Low operational risk in a localhost-only server, but a good hardening measure. Does not block approval.

Low — Input Validation / CHUNK_FILENAME_RE upper-bound: The allowlist regex /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/ has no maximum length constraint on the filename stem. A client could submit a 10,000-character filename that passes the regex, triggering a readFile() on a path that will not exist (benign ENOENT + 404), but consuming path-resolution overhead. Recommendation: add an early length check (e.g. if filename.length > 256) before the regex test, consistent with the MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH=128 pattern used for slugs. Minor hardening — does not block approval.

Low — A08 / .md cache poisoning via symlink: If an attacker with local filesystem access places a symlink at the expected mdPath location pointing to a sensitive file, the cache-first readFile() at L1604 would read and return the symlink target's contents. The CHUNK_FILENAME_RE + prefix check prevents the client from controlling which mdPath is chosen, so this requires pre-existing local filesystem write access to the chunks directory — at which point the system is already compromised. Noted for completeness; not a remotely exploitable vector in the threat model of a localhost server.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/api.ts (handleGetChunkText, ~60 lines) and mcp-server/gui/server.ts (route dispatch block, lines 984–1003).
All 7 acceptance criteria confirmed met — no blocking issues found across all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context).
One Fix-Forward applied: removed spurious double blank line after the renderChunksToText import in api.ts (line 72 → single blank line). Non-behavioral, cosmetic only.
Two documentation-forward items tagged for the Documentation agent.

Route ordering in server.ts is correct — the 6-segment /text route precedes the 5-segment /chunks/:filename route, preventing shadowing. Guard conditions (SAFE_SLUG_REGEX, rest[2] !== 'chunks', resolveRepoName) are identical to the /rendered sibling. Structural consistency is exemplary.

The defence-in-depth prefix check asymmetry (applied to mdPath but not the .jsonl filePath) is defensible: CHUNK_FILENAME_RE already mathematically bounds the .jsonl path, while the .md path is derived via string manipulation and warrants the extra guard. This asymmetry is intentional and architecturally sound.

The best-effort writeFile catch block (bare catch, no rethrow) is correctly positioned — it does not swallow errors from readFile or renderChunksToText, only from the cache-write side-effect. The error isolation boundary is precise.

The cache-first strategy (try readFile(mdPath) → ENOENT fall-through → extract → best-effort write) is clean and idiomatic. The ENOENT-only re-throw guard on the mdPath read (line 1607) correctly re-propagates unexpected errors (permissions, I/O failures) while only swallowing the expected cache-miss case.
PASS with Fix-Forward.

comments.note: Fix-Forward: Removed spurious double blank line between the 'import { renderChunksToText }' statement and the 'Internal helpers' section comment in api.ts (line 72). The rest of the file consistently uses a single blank line between the last import and the first section divider. Non-behavioral — QA validation remains fully intact.

[documentation-forward] handleGetChunkText() JSDoc (api.ts ~L1549) documents the NOT_FOUND throw cases but omits that a corrupt or unparseable .jsonl file causes renderChunksToText() to throw, which propagates as a 500 INTERNAL_ERROR (not a 404). Add a @throws entry: '@throws Internal server error (500) if the .jsonl content cannot be parsed by renderChunksToText().' This helps future contributors distinguish the two error surfaces.

[documentation-forward] The defence-in-depth prefix check in handleGetChunkText is applied to mdPath (the .md side) but not to filePath (the .jsonl side), which differs from the handleGetChunkFile sibling that does check the .jsonl path. This is intentional — CHUNK_FILENAME_RE already mathematically bounds the .jsonl filePath, while .md derivation via string replacement warrants the extra guard. Add a brief inline comment near line 1614 explaining this intentional asymmetry so future contributors do not add a redundant check or incorrectly perceive it as a missing one. E.g.: '// No prefix check needed here — CHUNK_FILENAME_RE already bounds the .jsonl filename to safe characters; mdPath requires a check because it is derived via string replacement.'

The server.ts route dispatch function continues to grow (the /text route is now the third in a family of chunk-related routes). The existing if-else chain is consistent with the file's established pattern, but the Developer's prior observation about a table-driven router stands. As routes accumulate, consider a refactor to a route-map structure to improve discoverability and reduce the risk of guard-condition drift between route families.
